newsitem.title: UK: UK wool prices set for 1997 upturn.
newsitem.headline: UK wool prices set for 1997 upturn.

text.p: An upturn in UK wool prices in 1997 will come on the back of a forecast recovery in domestic and west European carpet demand, a senior industry figure said.
In a recent report, British Wool Marketing Board chief Ian Hartley described the outlook for next year as "encouraging".

Recent trade shows on the Continent have boosted business confidence in the textile industry and seen woollen cloth and clothing manufacturers reporting more contracts available for the taking, he said.
"All these factors suggest a steady price increase through 1997, and I believe that is the case barring unforeseen events," Hartley said.
The planned increase in wool offered forward, which carries a premium, could also help to uplift UK prices.
The most unpredictable factor is the knock-on effect of global wool price movements which tend to be very volatile, particularly in the light of erratic market play by China.
The Board plans to continue with its push into the Chinese and Japanese markets in 1997 and is also looking at Nepal, Hartley said.
